_comment: Recorded ng on column for the 24 Colorado PAX8 runs, read from the instrument
description concentration ('N ug digested in 20 uL'). Keys are .raw folder stems.
NEITHER FACTOR WAS MEASURED. The volume is the programmed value and the
concentration is a typed sample description, so this is the intended load, not
an observed one. The trap uses partial-loop injection.
This is a CONSTANT-LOAD design: 1 uL x 0.5 ug/uL, 2 uL x 0.25 and 5 uL x 0.10
all put 500 ng on column. The 1:2:5 volumes do not span load.
Two file names contradict the record. PAX8_JP210_100ng_60_1uL and _120_1uL are
recorded at 0.2 uL, not 1 uL, which is how they reach 100 ng.
DISPUTED, see _disputed below: PAX8_JP213_100ng_60_0-5uL is recorded at 2.0 uL
of the 0.25 ug/uL vial, so 500 ng, against a name that says 100 ng at 0.5 uL.
If the method was simply left at 2.0 uL after a real 0.5 uL injection the true
value is 0.5 x 0.25 = 125 ng. It is not 100 ng either way, and this file does
60 min and 120 min are DIFFERENT LC METHODS. A load slope pooled across them
mixes method with load. Each method holds exactly one 100 ng run.

PAX8_JP213_100ng_60_0-5uL_20260924_4.why: 2.0 uL in the record against 0.5 uL in the name; 100 ng is wrong on both readings
